title: Fast gestures can cause a use-after-free crash in Phoc
description: We have found that certain touch gestures, especially when performed quickly, can cause Phoc to crash. Some specific gestures seem to trigger the crash more frequently than others. After extensive analysis and debugging, we found that Phoc could access a structure that had already been freed by wlroots. The issue appears to be related to the lifetime of `struct wlr_touch_point` in `phoc_cursor_handle_touch_up()`.\ \ Phoc retrieves a pointer to a `wlr_touch_point` and then calls `handle_gestures_for_event_at()`. During gesture handling, the touch point can be destroyed by wlroots. However, Phoc subsequently accesses `point->surface`, even though `point` is no longer valid.\ \ This results in a use-after-free, which can lead to an invalid surface pointer and eventually cause Phoc to crash. We found a working solution that prevents Phoc from crashing when performing these touch gestures. We started testing the fix a month ago and have not been able to reproduce the crash since. We have also not encountered any new issues related to this change during testing.

title: Research opportunities to avoid texture copies
description:
GTK uses wl_shm, which means that phoc ends up uploading every damaged part of the frame to GL domain with `glTex(Sub)Image2D`. Just keeping up with fullscreen updates of wl_shm surfaces makes phoc take more than 30% of devkit's CPU core time.

Given that we don't have dedicated VRAM, theoretically it might be possible to avoid copies and just share the shared memory buffer with the GL driver. Whether it's actually possible in practice remains to be seen.

More or less related reading:
- https://software.intel.com/en-us/articles/zero-copy-texture-uploads-in-chrome-os
- https://01.org/chromium/2016/native-one-copy-texture-uploads-for-chrome-OS
- https://arrayfire.com/zero-copy-on-integrated-gpus/
- https://events17.linuxfoundation.org/sites/events/files/slides/ELC17-virtmem-exp_0.pdf (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LFU39w7lY08) - code: https://github.com/jaychiang001/tda2_kernel/commit/c940bbbdfa32d492eddbc255459bc505dff7bef5
- anything related to dma_bufs

title: Incorrect key used when retrieving a sequence state
description:
In phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state(), the priv-\>points hash table is indexed by PhocEventSequence \*.\
\
When a point is added, it is stored using sequence as the key:\
\
g_hash_table_insert (priv-\>points, sequence, data);\
\
However, phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state() uses self as the key when looking up the corresponding PointData:\
\
data = g_hash_table_lookup (priv-\>points, self);\
\
Since self is a PhocGesture \* rather than a PhocEventSequence \*, the lookup cannot find the PointData associated with the sequence. As a result, the function returns PHOC_EVENT_SEQUENCE_NONE instead of the actual state of the sequence.\
\
The lookup should use sequence instead:\
\
data = g_hash_table_lookup (priv-\>points, sequence);\
\
This allows phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state() to correctly retrieve the PointData associated with the requested sequence and return its state.

So it make Phoc crash.

I found solution, I would like to fork and make a MR.

title: layer-shell-effects: Differentiate between user-initiated drag and compositor-initiated animation
description:
There's a TODO, but let's have an issue too:

```
    <event name="dragged">
      <description summary="A drag is ongoing">
        The is draging the surface.

        TODO: indicate drag (by user) vs slide (by compositor)
      </description>
      <arg name="margin" type="int" summary="The current margin"/>
    </event>
```

Not having that leads to phosh keeping the overview open when there's a single window which happens to unmap and map itself back quickly (like Waydroid often does). This happens because phosh [doesn't fold the overview when it's being dragged by the user](https://gitlab.gnome.org/World/Phosh/phosh/-/commit/0e80d0219c06), but it has no way to differentiate it from compositor's unfolding animation that's already running at that point.
